## Getting started

<a id="group-getting-started"></a>Group `getting-started`. **Goal:** Open Anita for the first time, understand that your data stays on your device and pick how to start your first project.

**Audience:** First-time users who have just opened Anita in a browser; no account, no setup, no technical knowledge.

**Notes for writers:** Home page material: no sign-up, no Anita server, data kept in your own browser (storage.local-database) — the core promise of privacy. Screenshots: the three steps of the introduction and the "Your first project" / "Choose a template" page. Explain the three ways to start (template, from scratch, import) and point to the template guide as the recommended one. Pitfall to say early, in plain words: data lives in one browser on one device, so clearing browsing data or using a private window loses it; link to "Keep your projects safe". Skip the technical details of the database (IndexedDB, one database per project): they are not for users. Mention "Show the introduction again".

### Introduction to Anita

`app.onboarding` · stable · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/onboarding/onboarding.component.tsx:277`

A welcome in three steps that explains what Anita does and asks how you want to start.

- **Where:** Shown at the first start, when there are no projects on the device; "Show the introduction again" link on the first
project page.
- **How:** 1. Click "Let's start" on the welcome step.
2. Read "What is Anita" and click "How do I start?".
3. Choose "Start from a template" (recommended), "Import my projects from Dropbox or WordPress", or "or start from
scratch with an empty project".
- **Options:** "Back", "Skip intro" (goes to the last step) and the step dots; the left and right arrow keys move between the steps.
- **Rules:** Choosing how to start marks the introduction as seen in this browser, so it is not shown again (if the browser blocks
storage it is shown again next time). Templates open the template gallery, import opens the "Storage and sync" screen,
scratch opens the empty project editor.
- **routes:** `projectsNone`
- **Related:** `project.first-project`, `template.gallery`, `project.create`

### Create your first project

`project.first-project` · stable · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/projects/no-projects.component.tsx:50`

When there are no projects on this device, the app shows the introduction and then the templates to create the first one.

- **Where:** Shown automatically when this device has no projects: "Your first project" / "Choose a template".
- **How:** 1. Go through the introduction (only the first time).
2. Pick a template, or "Start from scratch".
3. Or bring existing projects: "Open from Dropbox", "Import", or the link "I have projects in Dropbox or on WordPress".
- **Options:** "Show the introduction again" link at the bottom of the page.
- **Rules:** The introduction is shown until you choose how to start; afterwards this page opens directly on the templates. As soon
as there is a project on the device the app goes to the Projects list.
- **routes:** `projectsNone`
- **Related:** `app.onboarding`, `template.gallery`, `template.create-project`, `import.file`

### Where your data is kept

`storage.local-database` · stable · since 0.9.0 · `src/app/libs/db-connector/plugins/indexed-db/db-store/dbstore.class.ts:9`

Projects and records are saved in the browser of your device, without any Anita server.

- **Where:** Automatic; nothing to set. The data lives in the storage of the browser (IndexedDB) for the site of Anita.
- **How:** Nothing to do: every change is saved on the device as soon as you make it.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** Anita has no server: your data never leaves the device unless you sync it with Dropbox or WordPress, or export it.
The data belongs to one browser on one device: another browser, another device or a private window does not see it. To use the same projects elsewhere, sync or export them.
The list of projects is kept in one database of the browser; each project has its own database with a table per section.
Removing a section from a project deletes its records from the device; deleting a project deletes its database from the device.
Clearing the site data or the history of the browser (or private windows being closed) deletes the data kept on the device: keep a copy with sync or export.
- **Related:** `app.offline`

## Start from a ready-made template

<a id="group-start-from-a-template"></a>Group `start-from-a-template`. **Goal:** Find a template that fits what you want to keep track of and create a working project from it in one click, with example records if you like.

**Audience:** New users who have seen the introduction and want something working right away.

**Notes for writers:** Follow one example through the guide, e.g. the Recipes template (or a simple CRM): browse the gallery, search, open it, look at "What's inside", tick "Start with some example records", create. Screenshots: the gallery with the category tabs and search, the page of a template with the form and "What's inside", the new project with its example records. Explain the "Where to save it" choice only briefly and link to "Keep your projects safe" and the Dropbox / WordPress guides. Pitfalls: example records are real records (delete them when done); "Customize the structure first" creates the project without examples; offline the gallery shows only the templates saved on the device. Home page: "dozens of ready-made templates" is a good hook.

### Browse the templates

`template.gallery` · stable · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/templates/template-gallery.component.tsx:106`

A gallery of ready-made projects (tasks, CRM, budget, recipes...), by category and with search.

- **Where:** "Create a project" page (from "New project") and the first project page ("Choose a template").
- **How:** 1. Type in "Search templates" or pick a category.
2. Click a template to see what is inside and create the project.
- **Options:** Category tabs ("All" and each category, with the number of templates). Search box. "Start from scratch" card, shown
in "All" when nothing is searched.
- **Rules:** Each card shows the name, category, description and sections of the template. The search looks in names,
descriptions, tags and section names; with no result: "No template matches your search. Try other words, or start
from scratch.". Templates are downloaded from the Anita catalog and the last copy is kept on the device: offline the
gallery says "You are offline: showing the templates saved on this device.". If they cannot be downloaded and no copy
is saved: "The templates could not be downloaded..." with "Try again" and "Start from scratch". Templates change
without updating the app; self-hosted installations can use their own catalog (set when the app is built).
- **routes:** `projectNew`, `projectsNone`
- **Related:** `template.create-project`, `project.create`, `project.first-project`

### Create a project from a template

`template.create-project` · stable · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/templates/create-from-template.component.tsx:315`

Preview the sections and fields of a template, name the project, choose where to save it and create it in one click.

- **Where:** Click a template in the gallery: page with the form and "What's inside"; "All templates" goes back to the gallery.
- **How:** 1. Look at "What's inside": sections, their fields and links between sections.
2. Change "Project name" and "Description" if you want.
3. Choose "Where to save it".
4. Click "Create project" ("Create and connect Dropbox" or "Create and connect WordPress" when a login is needed), or
"Customize the structure first" to change sections and fields in the editor before creating it.
- **Options:** Project name and description (default: those of the template). "Start with some example records". Where to save it:
only this device, Dropbox, a connected WordPress site or a new WordPress site; a connected Dropbox or site is proposed
when there is one.
- **Rules:** The name is required ("Give the project a name."). When Dropbox or the site needs a login, the browser leaves the app
and the project is linked when you come back; "Customize the structure first" is then disabled. The address of a new
site is checked before anything is saved. Problems are shown in "The project was not created". A template that is no
longer in the catalog shows "This template is no longer available."; if the catalog cannot be downloaded, "The
template could not be downloaded." with "Try again". After creation the project opens.
- **routes:** `projectNewFromTemplate`
- **errors:** `wordpress.network`, `wordpress.pluginMissing`, `wordpress.originNotAllowed`, `dropbox.network`, `dropbox.authFailed`
- **Related:** `template.gallery`, `template.sample-records`, `project.create`, `section.add`

`template.sample-records` · stable · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/templates/create-from-template.component.tsx:97`

Fills a project created from a template with a few realistic records, already linked to each other, to see how
everything works.

- **Where:** "Start with some example records" checkbox on the page of a template.
- **How:** 1. Open a template from the gallery.
2. Tick or untick "Start with some example records".
3. Create the project.
- **Options:** Ticked by default when there are no projects on the device yet, unticked otherwise.
- **Rules:** Shown only for templates that come with examples. Dates of the examples are set relative to the day the project is

## Find your way around

<a id="group-find-your-way-around"></a>Group `find-your-way-around`. **Goal:** Move between your projects and their sections, keep the menu tidy and use the shortcuts that make Anita quicker.

**Audience:** Users who have created their first project and want to know where everything is.

**Notes for writers:** Use the project created in the template guide. Start from the Projects screen (cards, "Load project", "Open project"), then the project page, the sidebar with its sections and the project picker at the top; then the small comforts: Anita reopens the last project, hide sections you rarely use, bookmark any page and use the browser's Back button. Screenshots: Projects screen with two or three cards, the sidebar on desktop and the menu button on a phone, the open project picker, the "Edit menu" gear. End with a reference table of all keyboard shortcuts gathered from the catalogue: C (new record, on a section list), E (edit, on a record), Escape (close / cancel), Mod+S (save a record), Mod+B / Mod+I / Mod+U / Mod+` (text styles in a long text); explain that Mod is Cmd on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere, and that single-key shortcuts do nothing while typing. Pitfall: a page address only works on this device — sending it to someone does not share the record. Mention the "Report a bug" link and the version number at the bottom of the sidebar. Dialogs need only a short paragraph (red buttons mean something is deleted).

### See and open your projects

`project.list` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/projects/projects-list.component.tsx:13`

The list of the projects saved on this device, with where each one is stored and the actions on it.

- **Where:** "Projects" screen ("On this device"), one card per project.
- **How:** 1. Open the Projects screen.
2. On the card of a project click "Load project".
3. Click "Open project" to go to its details, or use "Export" and "Edit Project" on the card.
- **Options:** Buttons of the screen: "Storage and sync" (connect Dropbox or WordPress sites), "Open from Dropbox", "Import" and
"New project". Buttons of each card: "Delete Project", "Load project", then "Export", "Edit Project" and "Open project".
- **Rules:** Each card shows the avatar, name and description of the project, its creation date and where it is synced: "Synced
with Dropbox", "Synced with" and the name of the WordPress site, or the warning "Only on this device, no backup · Keep
it safe", which opens the dialog to save the project in Dropbox or on a WordPress site. "Export", "Edit Project" and
"Open project" appear once the project is loaded. When there are no projects the app shows the first project page.
- **routes:** `projectsList`
- **Related:** `project.first-project`, `project.create`, `project.delete`, `export.project`, `import.file`

### Project info page

`project.info-page` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/project/details.component.tsx:9`

Shows the main information of the open project and the buttons to edit, export or delete it.

- **Where:** Sidebar, project menu at the top: "Details" (or click the current project); on the projects list, "Open project" on a project card. It is also the page that opens after creating, importing or opening a project.
- **How:** Open the project menu in the sidebar and choose "Details". Read the information, then use the buttons at the bottom of the card.
- **Options:** Buttons at the bottom of the card: "Delete Project", "Export" (Data and Structure, Data Only, Structure Only) and "Edit Project".

### Sidebar and sections menu

`navigation.sidebar` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/admin-layout/admin-layout-sidebar.component.tsx:11`

The menu on the left that lists the sections of the open project and takes you to their records.

- **Where:** Left side of every page while a project is open; on phones it is hidden behind the menu button (three lines) at the top left of the header.
- **How:** 1. Open a project.
2. Click a section under "Sections" to see its records.

- **Rules:** The sidebar appears only when a project is open; on the projects list with no project it is not shown.

Each section shows its icon (a chevron when it has none) and its short name when one is set, otherwise its full name; long names are cut.
The section you are viewing is highlighted.
Sections hidden from the menu are not listed (see "Show or hide sections in the menu").
On wide screens the sidebar is always visible; on small screens it slides in over the page and closes after you pick a section.
At the bottom it shows the version of Anita ("v" and the number) and a bug icon ("Report a bug") that opens the Anita issues page on GitHub in a new tab.

### Switch project from the sidebar

`navigation.project-picker` · stable · since 0.10.0 · `src/app/components/admin-layout/admin-layout-sidebar-project-picker.component.tsx:20`

A menu at the top of the sidebar to see the open project, open its details or settings, switch to another project or create a new one.

- **Where:** Top of the sidebar: the box with the initial of the project, its name and how many sections it has.
- **How:** 1. Click the project box at the top of the sidebar.
2. Choose an item of the menu: the current project or "Details" opens its details page, "Edit" opens its settings, a project under "Switch to" opens it, "Go to the projects list" or "Create a new project" open those pages.

### Reopen the last project

`navigation.reopen-last-project` · stable · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/admin-layout/admin-layout.component.tsx:29`

When you come back to Anita, the project you used last is opened again in the sidebar.

- **Where:** Automatic, when Anita starts on a page that is not inside a project (for example the projects list).
- **How:** Nothing to do: open or reload Anita and the sidebar shows the last project you opened.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** Anita remembers on this device the last project you opened; if that project no longer exists, the first project of the list is opened; with no projects nothing is opened.
Pages inside a project (their address starts with /project/) open the project of their address instead.
The remembered project is per browser: other browsers or devices remember their own.
- **Related:** `navigation.project-picker`

### Show or hide sections in the menu

`navigation.hide-sections-in-menu` · stable · since 0.16.0 · `src/app/components/admin-layout/admin-layout-sidebar-edit-menu-button.component.tsx:10`

Hide from the sidebar the sections you do not use often, and show them again when needed.

- **Where:** Sidebar, gear button ("Edit menu") next to the label "Sections".
- **How:** 1. Click the gear button next to "Sections": every section, also the hidden ones, gets an eye icon.
2. Click the eye of a section to hide it (crossed eye, tooltip "Show") or to show it again (open eye, tooltip "Hide").
3. Click the check button that replaced the gear to finish: hidden sections disappear from the menu.
- **Options:** Each section is shown by default.
- **Rules:** Hiding a section only removes it from the menu: its records are kept and can still be reached, for example from links of other records.
The choice is saved in the project structure, so it is kept after a reload and travels with the project when it is synced or exported.
- **Related:** `navigation.sidebar`

### Page addresses and the Back button

`navigation.addresses` · stable · since 0.2.4 · `src/app/libs/routing/anita-routes.component.tsx:90`

Every page of Anita has its own address, so you can bookmark it, reload it and go back with the browser's Back button.

- **Where:** The address bar of the browser (addresses look like .../#/project/.../list/...); the Back and Forward buttons of the browser or of the phone.
- **How:** Use the Back and Forward buttons, bookmark a page, or reload it: Anita opens the same page.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** The part of the address after # says which page is open: the projects list, a project, a section list, a record, a form.
The address of the app itself (/) and unknown addresses open the projects list.
A page of a project shows a loader while the project opens; if the project does not exist on this device (for example a link from another device or a deleted project), Anita opens the projects list.
An address points to data on this device only: sending it to someone else does not share the record.
Pages change with a short animation; the header and the sidebar stay in place.
- **routes:** `projectsList`
- **Related:** `navigation.sidebar`

### Dialogs and confirmations

`navigation.dialogs` · stable · since 0.7.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/modals/modal.component.tsx:131`

Questions and confirmations open in a window over the page, with the action buttons at the bottom.

- **Where:** Over any page, when an action needs an answer (for example deleting, or a choice during a sync).
- **How:** 1. Read the title and the text of the dialog.
2. Click the button of the action you want, or "Cancel" to do nothing.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** Only one dialog is open at a time and it covers the whole app, header included; the page behind is dimmed.
The action buttons are at the bottom right, "Cancel" before them; some dialogs have no "Cancel" or have an extra button on the left. A button can be disabled until the dialog is filled in.
Dialogs for dangerous actions (such as deleting) show a red warning icon and a red action button.
A dialog is at most as tall as the window: title and buttons stay visible and the content scrolls.
Most dialogs close only with their buttons; some (such as the sync questions) also close, as a cancel, with Escape or a click outside.

### Keyboard shortcuts

`navigation.keyboard-shortcuts` · stable · since 0.18.1 · `src/app/libs/shortcuts/shortcuts-listener.ts:6`

Some actions can be done from the keyboard; the shortcuts follow the same rules everywhere in the app.

- **Where:** Anywhere in the app with a keyboard; each shortcut works on the page that offers it.
- **How:** Press the keys of the shortcut while the page that offers it is open.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** Mod means Cmd on macOS and Ctrl on Windows, Linux and other systems.
Letters work in upper or lower case.
Shortcuts made of a single key are ignored while you type in a text box (single-line or multi-line), so typing a letter never triggers them; shortcuts with Mod work also while typing.
A shortcut works only while the page or panel that offers it is shown; when two open parts offer the same keys, the one opened last wins.

## Add and update your records

<a id="group-add-and-edit-records"></a>Group `add-and-edit-records`. **Goal:** Add the things you keep track of, look at their details, change them and remove the ones you no longer need.

**Audience:** Users with a project open (from a template or built by themselves) who want to fill it in.

**Notes for writers:** Continue the example of the template guide: add a recipe (or a client), save it, open its details, edit it, tick a checkbox such as "Done" straight from the table, delete a test record. Screenshots: the round "+" button, the add form with a required field marked by the asterisk and the message next to the save buttons, the details page, the pencil button. Explain the difference between "Save" (stays in the form, only when the section has a long text) and "Save & Close", and that the form cannot be saved while a required field is empty or a value is marked in red (details in the fields guide). Shortcuts to mention: C, E, Mod+S, Escape. Pitfall: deleting a record cannot be undone. Linking a record to others ("Linked to") is only hinted at here and explained in "Link records to each other".

### Add a record

`record.add` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/element/add-edit.component.tsx:19`

Creates a new record in a section by filling in a form with the fields of the section.

- **Where:** List of a section: the round "+" button at the bottom right (its label "New record" appears on hover), or "Create a new entry" when the section is empty. Details page of a record with child sections: "Add to" followed by the name of the child section.
- **How:** Click "+" (or press C), fill in the fields, then click "Save" or "Save & Close".
- **Options:** In a section that is a child of other sections, a "Linked to" selector at the top of the form links the new record to records of the parent sections. When the form is opened from the tab of a child section on a details page, the new record is already linked to that record.
- **Rules:** The form header reads "Add to" followed by the section name. Required fields are marked with an asterisk. The C shortcut works on the list of a section.
- **routes:** `projectSectionAddEle`
- **shortcuts:** `C`
- **Related:** `record.save`, `record.edit`, `view.child-records-tabs`

### Save or cancel a record

`record.save` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/element/add-edit-save-cancel-buttons.component.tsx:33`

Saves the record being added or edited, or leaves the form without saving.

- **Where:** Bottom of the add and edit forms of a record: "Cancel", "Save" and "Save & Close".
- **How:** Click "Save & Close" (or "Save" in sections without a rich text field) to save and go back to the previous page. In sections with a rich text field, "Save" saves and keeps the form open. Press Mod+S to save without leaving the form. Click "Cancel" or press Escape to go back without saving.
- **Options:** "Save" (stay in the form, only in sections with a rich text field), "Save & Close", "Cancel".
- **Rules:** The save buttons and Mod+S do nothing while the form is not valid: next to the buttons a message lists the missing required fields ("To save, fill in the required field: ...") or reads "To save, correct the fields marked in red.". Empty values are not stored. The record is saved on this device first, then synced when the project is on Dropbox or WordPress.
- **routes:** `projectSectionAddEle`, `projectSectionEditEle`
- **shortcuts:** `Mod+S`, `Escape`
- **Related:** `record.add`, `record.edit`

`record.details` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/element/details.component.tsx:124`

Shows all the values of a record, the records it is linked to, and the buttons to edit or delete it.

- **Where:** List of a section: click a row of the table or a card of the grid. Also from the links to linked records.
- **How:** Open a record from the list. Read its values; click a linked record to open it; press Escape to go back.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** The header is the name of the record ("Details" when it has none), with the section name above it. Each field is shown with its label; empty fields are not shown and long texts take the whole row. Checkbox fields can be ticked directly. If the record no longer exists, the list of the section opens.

- **shortcuts:** `Escape`

- **Rules:** The form header reads "Edit" followed by the name of the record as it was saved ("Edit record" when it has no name). The form shows a loader until the record is read. The E shortcut works on the details page of a record.

- **Related:** `record.details`

## See your records the way you need

<a id="group-see-your-records"></a>Group `see-your-records`. **Goal:** Look at the records of a section as a table or as cards, sort them and choose which columns to show.

**Audience:** Users who already have some records in a section.

**Notes for writers:** Use a section with at least six or seven records (the example records of a template are ideal). Show the list of a section, switch between table and cards, sort by a date or a name column, hide a column you do not need. Screenshots: the same section as table and as grid side by side; the sort arrow on a header; the "Edit visible columns" window. Tell users that view, sorting and visible columns are saved with the project, so they are the same on other devices and for the people the project is shared with. Explain what a card shows (name, up to two choice fields, the first date, the first long text as description) so users know which fields to add to get nice cards. Pitfall: hiding a column never deletes data. The "Edit Card Layout" window of the grid has no settings yet: do not document it as a feature.

### List of the records of a section

`view.section-list` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/list/list.component.tsx:16`

Shows all the records of a section of the project, as a table or as cards.

- **Where:** Sidebar: click the name of a section of the open project.
- **How:** Click a section in the sidebar. The page shows the section title, the project name above it and the number of records; click a record to open its details, or the round "+" button at the bottom right to add one.
- **Options:** The records can be shown as a table or as cards (grid); the view chosen last is kept for each section.
- **Rules:** Records are listed in the order they were created (the table can be sorted by a column instead). When the section has no records, the page reads "Nothing here yet" and "There are no items in" followed by the section name, with a "Create a new entry" button. The list updates by itself when records change, also after a sync. If the section does not exist, the app goes back to the projects list.
- **routes:** `projectSectionElesList`
- **Related:** `view.table`, `view.grid`, `view.switch-view`, `record.add`, `record.details`

### Switch between table and cards

`view.switch-view` · stable · since 0.14.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/list/tabs/header-right-view-selector.component.tsx:14`

Chooses whether the records of a section are shown as a table or as cards.

- **Where:** List of a section: the two icons at the top right of the list (table, grid).
- **How:** Click the table icon to see the records as a table, or the grid icon to see them as cards.
- **Options:** Table (default) or grid of cards.
- **Rules:** The choice is remembered for each section and saved in the project, so it is the same on the other devices and for the other users the project is synced with. A white marker slides under the selected icon.
- **routes:** `projectSectionElesList`
- **covers:** `view:table`, `view:grid`
- **Related:** `view.table`, `view.grid`

### Table view

`view.table` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/list/table/table-container.component.tsx:52`

Shows the records of a section as rows of a table, one column per field.

- **Where:** List of a section, with the table icon selected at the top right (the default view).
- **How:** Open a section from the sidebar. Click a row to open the details of the record; tick a checkbox directly in its cell to change it.
- **Options:** Which columns are shown (gear icon "Edit view") and the column used for sorting (click a header).
- **Rules:** The first column, in bold, is the field that names the records. When the pointer is over a row, an arrow appears at its end. Rows appear one after the other with a short animation. Long values stay on one line and a wide table scrolls sideways. Rich text and other values are shown as on the details page.
- **routes:** `projectSectionElesList`
- **covers:** `view:table`
- **Related:** `view.table-columns`, `view.table-sort`, `view.switch-view`, `record.title`, `record.inline-checkbox`

### Sort a table by a column

`view.table-sort` · stable · since 0.16.2 · `src/app/components/project/section/list/table/table-container.component.tsx:14`

Orders the records of a table by the values of one column.

- **Where:** List of a section, table view: the column headers.
- **How:** Click a column header to sort by it in ascending order; click it again to switch to descending order. Click another header to sort by that column.
- **Options:** Ascending or descending, on one column at a time. Without a choice, records are in the order they were created.
- **Rules:** An arrow next to the header shows the sorted column and the direction. Empty values go last. The sorting is saved for each section in the project, so it is kept when you come back and is synced with the project.
- **routes:** `projectSectionElesList`
- **covers:** `view:table`
- **Related:** `view.table`

### Show or hide columns of a table

`view.table-columns` · stable · since 0.16.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/list/tabs/header-right-edit-view-table.component.tsx:22`

Chooses which fields of a section appear as columns in its table.

- **Where:** List of a section, table view: the gear icon "Edit view" at the top right, then the "Edit visible columns" window.
- **How:** Click the gear icon, switch on or off the field you want to show or hide, then click "Close".
- **Options:** One switch per field of the section; all fields are shown by default. The "Add field" button in the same window adds a new field to the section.
- **Rules:** Changes apply at once and are saved in the project (they are synced with it). Hiding a column does not delete any data. The field that names the records stays the first column when it is shown.
- **routes:** `projectSectionElesList`
- **covers:** `view:table`
- **Related:** `view.table`, `view.add-field`

### Grid (cards) view

`view.grid` · stable · since 0.14.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/list/grid/grid.tsx:19`

Shows the records of a section as cards, with their name, a few short values and a description.

- **Where:** List of a section, with the grid icon selected at the top right.
- **How:** Click the grid icon above the list. Click a card to open the details of the record.
- **Options:** none (the gear icon "Edit view" opens an "Edit Card Layout" window that has no settings yet).
- **Rules:** Each card shows the field that names the records as its title ("Untitled" when empty), then up to two choice fields (drop-down or radio buttons) and the first date field when they have a value, then the first rich text field of the section as description. Long descriptions are cut, with a fade only when they are actually cut. Cards are arranged in 1 to 4 columns depending on the width of the screen.
- **routes:** `projectSectionElesList`
- **covers:** `view:grid`
- **Related:** `view.switch-view`, `record.title`

## Build your own project

<a id="group-build-your-own-project"></a>Group `build-your-own-project`. **Goal:** Create a project from scratch, or adapt one, by choosing its sections (the kinds of things you track) and the fields of each; change it later or delete it.

**Audience:** Users who know how to add records and want a project shaped on their own needs; no database knowledge.

**Notes for writers:** Follow one example from scratch, e.g. a reading list: project "My books" with sections "Books" and "Authors", a few fields per section. Explain sections as "the kinds of things you keep track of" and fields as "the information you write down for each" — avoid words like schema, table or entity. Screenshots: "Create a project" page with "Start from scratch", the editor with the top card (name, description, remote storage), a section card with its fields, "Add section" / "Add field". Show also the quick way to add a field from the list (gear "Edit view" → "Add field"). Advanced mode: one short paragraph, for users who need identifiers or stored values; most users never need it. Pitfalls: a field once saved keeps its identifier; deleting a section or a field in the editor deletes its data when you save; on a project shared on WordPress only the owner and administrators can edit or delete it. Deleting a project: explain the three cases of the confirmation (only this device, Dropbox — goes to Dropbox's deleted files, WordPress — gone for everyone) and that it cannot be undone; suggest an export first. Field types are in the next guide; parent sections in "Link records to each other".

### Create a project

`project.create` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/templates/new-project.component.tsx:6`

Start a new project from a template, from scratch or from a file.

- **Where:** "New project" button of the Projects screen, which opens the "Create a project" page; its "Start from scratch" card
opens the empty "Add Project" editor.
- **How:** 1. On the Projects screen click "New project".
2. Pick a template, click "Start from scratch" to design your own sections and fields, or click "Import" to load a
project file.
3. From scratch: fill in the project info, define the sections and their fields, then click "Save".
- **Options:** A template, a blank project ("Start from scratch") or an import. In the editor: where to store the project and
"Advanced mode".
- **Rules:** A new project is saved in the browser of this device and, if a remote storage is chosen, synced there too. "Save"
stays disabled while a required field is empty or invalid; "Cancel" goes back without creating anything. After
saving, the project opens. If the templates cannot be downloaded the page offers "Try again" and "Start from scratch".
- **routes:** `projectNew`, `projectAdd`
- **Related:** `template.gallery`, `template.create-project`, `import.file`, `project.settings`, `section.add`, `section.fields`

### Name and describe a project

`project.settings` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/data/project-form-builder/project-info-builder.constant.ts:57`

The name, description and remote storage of a project, set at the top of the project editor.

- **Where:** Top card of the "Add Project" / "Edit Project" editor, and the "Import project" dialog.
- **How:** 1. Type the name in "Project" and a short text in "Description".
2. Optionally choose a "Remote storage".
3. Save.
- **Options:** "Remote storage": none (only this browser), Dropbox, a connected WordPress site or a file on this computer.
Its hint only names the choices; a box under the field explains how the chosen one works (where the project is
saved, which devices get it, who can see it, and for a file that the browser asks permission at each visit).
- **Rules:** "Project" and "Description" are required: "Save" stays disabled while they are empty. The name is shown on the project
card and in the app, and names the export files.
- **Related:** `project.create`, `project.edit`, `import.file`

### Add sections to a project

`section.add` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/projects/add-edit-project-components/section-manager.component.tsx:20`

Sections are the kinds of records of a project (tasks, clients, books...): add them, name them and give them an icon
and a short name for the menu.

- **Where:** Project editor ("Add Project" / "Edit Project"): one card per section ("Section 1", "Section 2"...), "Add section"
button at the bottom, "Delete section" in each card.
- **How:** 1. Click "Add section".
2. Fill in the "Title" and, if you want, the "Abbreviation" and the "Icon".
3. Add the fields of the section.
4. Save the project.
- **Options:** "Abbreviation": used in the menu instead of the title, if set. "Icon": shown with the section in the menu. "Parent
sections:" to make it the child of other sections, so that its records can be linked to theirs.
- **Rules:** The title is required; the card shows "New section" until it has one. A new project starts with one empty section.
"Delete section" appears only when the project has more than one section. Sections keep the order in which they are
listed in the editor.
- **Related:** `section.fields`, `project.edit`, `project.create`

### Add fields to a section

`section.fields` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/projects/add-edit-project-components/section-form-model-manager.component.tsx:33`

Defines the fields of the records of a section: their label, data type and whether they must be filled.

- **Where:** Project editor ("Add Project" / "Edit Project"), "Section element fields" of each section card, with the "Add field" and
"Delete field" buttons.
- **How:** 1. In a section card click "Add field".
2. Type the "Field label".
3. Choose the "Data type"; for text fields also the "Content type", for dates the "Date format", for date and time the
"Time format".
4. For drop-down and alternative choice fields, type the "Choices".
5. Tick "Required" if the field must always be filled.
6. Save the project.
- **Options:** Data type: any field type of Anita (default: the first of the list). Content type of text fields (text, email,
number, phone, link, color...), date format, time format. "Required", off by default. "Identifier", only in Advanced
mode.
- **Rules:** The label is required. In basic mode the identifier is created from the label and kept unique in the section; once
the field is saved its identifier cannot be changed, while label, type and the other settings can. A new section
starts with one empty field; "Delete field" appears only when the section has more than one field.
- **Related:** `section.add`, `project.advanced-editor`

### Add a field from the list

`view.add-field` · stable · since 0.17.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/list/tabs/header-right-add-field.component.tsx:19`

Adds a new field to a section without opening the project editor.

- **Where:** List of a section, table view: gear icon "Edit view", then "Add field" at the bottom of the "Edit visible columns" window.
- **How:** Click "Add field", fill in the new field (name, type and its settings) in the "Add field" window, then click "Add". Click "Cancel" to close without adding.
- **Options:** The same field types and settings as in the project editor.
- **Rules:** "Add" is disabled while the new field is not valid (for example without a name). The field is added at the end of the section and the project is saved; existing records have no value for it until they are edited.
- **routes:** `projectSectionElesList`
- **Related:** `view.table-columns`

### Edit a project

`project.edit` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/projects/add-edit-project.component.tsx:16`

Change the name, description, storage, sections and fields of an existing project.

- **Where:** "Edit Project" button on the card of a loaded project (Projects screen) and on the details page of the project; it opens
the "Edit Project" editor.
- **How:** 1. Click "Edit Project".
2. Change the project info, add, change or delete sections and fields.
3. Click "Save", or "Cancel" to leave without changes.
- **Options:** "Advanced mode" toggle, to see and set identifiers and stored values.
- **Rules:** It is the same editor used for a new project ("Add Project"), headed "Edit Project". "Save" stays disabled while a
required field is empty or invalid. If the project does not exist (old link, deleted project) the app goes back to the
Projects list. The identifier of a field that already exists cannot be changed, so its records keep their values.
Sections and fields deleted in the editor are removed from the structure of the project when you save. On a project
shared on a WordPress site, only its owner and the administrators of the site see "Edit Project". Saved changes are
synced to Dropbox or to the WordPress site if the project is stored there. After saving, the project opens.
- **routes:** `projectEdit`
- **Related:** `project.create`, `project.settings`, `section.add`, `section.fields`, `project.advanced-editor`

### Advanced mode of the project editor

`project.advanced-editor` · stable · since 0.8.0 · `src/app/components/projects/add-edit-project-components/project-editor-mode-toggle.component.tsx:8`

Shows the technical settings of the fields: the identifier of each field and the stored value of each choice.

- **Where:** "Advanced mode" toggle at the top right of the "Add Project" / "Edit Project" editor.
- **How:** 1. Turn on "Advanced mode".
2. Set the "Identifier" of new fields and the "Value" of the choices of drop-down and choice fields.
- **Options:** Off by default (basic mode): identifiers are created from the field labels and choice values are numbered automatically.
- **Rules:** Identifiers of fields that already exist are shown but cannot be changed. The mode stays as set until the app is
reloaded.
- **Related:** `section.fields`, `project.edit`

### Delete a project

`project.delete` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/models/project/project-deletor.class.ts:19`

Removes a project and all its records from this device and, if it is synced, from the WordPress site, or from Dropbox if you confirm it.

- **Where:** "Delete Project" button on the card of the project (Projects screen).
- **How:** 1. Click "Delete Project".
2. Read the confirmation and click "Delete" (for Dropbox: "Delete from this device only" or "Delete also from Dropbox").
- **Options:** For a project synced with a file on this computer, the file is never deleted. For a project synced with Dropbox: "Delete from this device only" keeps its file in your Dropbox, "Delete also from Dropbox" moves the file to the deleted files of your Dropbox. Nothing is deleted from Dropbox without this explicit choice.
- **Rules:** The confirmation says what happens: for a project only on this device, all its data is removed from this device and
copies on other devices are not affected; for Dropbox, the dialog asks whether to delete the file in your Dropbox too:
with "Delete from this device only" the file stays in Dropbox, your other devices keep syncing it, and this device no
longer downloads it automatically ("Open from Dropbox" brings it back); with "Delete also from Dropbox" the file is
moved to the deleted files of your Dropbox (where it can be restored for a while) and your other devices ask what to
do with their copy; for WordPress, it is deleted
from the site and from this device, for every user it is shared with. On WordPress only the owner of the project and
the administrators of the site see the button. If the deletion on Dropbox or WordPress fails, "The project was not
deleted" explains why and the project is kept on this device. It cannot be undone. Afterwards the Projects list opens.
- **errors:** `wordpress.forbidden`, `wordpress.network`, `dropbox.network`, `dropbox.authFailed`
- **Related:** `project.list`, `export.project`

## Choose the right fields for your data

<a id="group-choose-field-types"></a>Group `choose-field-types`. **Goal:** Pick the right kind of field for each piece of information — text, notes, dates, check boxes, lists of choices — and make sure records are filled in correctly.

**Audience:** Users building or changing a project in the editor, who wonder which data type to pick.

**Notes for writers:** Best written as a gallery: one short block per field type with a screenshot of how it looks in the form and how it is shown in the list / details. Example to follow: a "Contacts" section with Name (short text), Email and Phone (short text with content type), Birthday (date), Notes (long text), Category (drop-down), Priority (alternative choice), Active (check box). Explain early that the first short text of type Text gives each record its name (bold first column, card title, page header) — so put the name field first. A table "which field for what" helps: few choices → alternative choice, many → drop-down. Pitfalls to warn about: the phone check accepts only numbers of ten digits grouped 3-3-4 and refuses international prefixes such as +39; web addresses must start with http:// or https://; deleting a choice empties it in the records that used it, renaming it does not; in the drop-down, typing searches the stored value (1, 2, 3…) and not the label; a Password field is only hidden on screen; Range has no settings; a required Long text does not actually block saving. Long text formatting: show the toolbar and the shortcuts Mod+B / I / U / `.

### Short text field

`field.short-text` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/input-supported-types.const.ts:3`

A one-line field for names, numbers, e-mail addresses, phone numbers, web addresses, passwords, colours or a value on a slider.

- **Where:** Project editor: a field of a section with Data type "Short text" and a "Content type". Filled in the form to add or edit a record; shown in the table and grid views, on the details page and in the tabs of linked records.
- **How:** In the project editor, give the field the Data type "Short text" and choose its Content type. When adding or editing a record, type the value in the box (Color opens a colour picker, Range shows a slider). Save the record.
- **Options:** Content type (default Text): Text, any text; Email, an e-mail address (example shown in the box: name@example.com), displayed as a link that starts a new e-mail; Number, only numbers, with arrows to increase or decrease; Password, hidden while typing and displayed as asterisks with an eye button to reveal it; Color, picked from the colour picker of the browser, displayed as a coloured dot; Range, a slider from 0 to 100, displayed as a percentage (e.g. 40%); Tel, a phone number (example: +1 555 0100), displayed as a link that starts a call; Url, a web address (example: https://), displayed as a link without "https://" and "www." that opens in a new tab.
- **Rules:** The label is shown above the box: the grey text inside it is only an example of the format. Email, Tel and Url values are checked while typing (see the check of e-mail, phone and web addresses). An empty value is not saved. A Password is hidden only on screen: it is stored like the other values of the record. Range has no minimum, maximum or step to set, and saves nothing until the slider is moved. The first Short text field of type Text (or the first required one) names the records of the section.
- **covers:** `field:basicInput`, `input-type:text`, `input-type:email`, `input-type:number`, `input-type:password`, `input-type:color`, `input-type:range`, `input-type:tel`, `input-type:url`
- **Related:** `field.format-validation`, `field.required`, `record.title`

### The field that names the records

`record.title` · stable · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/models/section/title-field.function.ts:10`

Each record is named after one of its fields (for example the name of a client), chosen automatically, without any setting.

- **Where:** Everywhere a record is named: first, bold column of tables (also of the linked records on a details page), title of the cards in the grid view, header of the details page, header of the edit form ("Edit" followed by the name), links to linked records and the "Linked to" selector of the form.
- **How:** Nothing to set: to choose the field that names the records, put a Short text field (Content type Text) first in the section in the project editor, or make it required.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** The name field is the first field of the section when it is a Short text of type Text; otherwise the first required Short text of type Text. Lists show it as the first column, whatever the order of the fields. When the section has no such field, lists keep the order of the fields and use the first field where a name is needed (grid cards, "Linked to" field); the details page reads "Details" and the edit form "Edit record". Spaces at the beginning and end are ignored; a record whose name is empty has no title in its header and is shown as "Untitled" in the links to it.
- **routes:** `projectSectionElesList`, `projectSectionEleDetails`, `projectSectionEditEle`
- **Related:** `field.short-text`, `relation.link-to-parent`, `view.table`, `view.grid`, `record.details`

### Long text field

`field.long-text` · stable · since 0.18.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/form-fields/rich-text.component.tsx:10`

A multi-line field with formatting (bold, headings, lists...) for notes, descriptions and any longer text.

- **Where:** Project editor: a field with Data type "Long text". Filled with a text editor with a toolbar in the form to add or edit a record; shown formatted on the details page, in the lists and as the description of the cards in grid view.
- **How:** In the project editor, give the field the Data type "Long text". When adding or editing a record, click in the editor (it shows "Enter text…" when empty), write, and format the text with the toolbar or the keyboard shortcuts. Save the record.
- **Options:** none: there is no Content type. The formatting available is described in "Format a long text".
- **Rules:** The text is saved with its formatting. A value written as plain text (e.g. imported, or saved before long texts had formatting) opens as a single paragraph. When a section has a Long text field, the form has two buttons: "Save", which keeps the form open, and "Save & Close"; otherwise there is only "Save". In grid view the first Long text field of the section is the description of each card, faded at the bottom when it is cut. Long texts are not shown in the tabs of linked records. The spell checker of the browser is active. If the field is required, its label shows the asterisk but the record can be saved with the editor empty.
- **covers:** `field:richText`
- **Related:** `field.rich-text-formatting`, `field.required`

### Format a long text

`field.rich-text-formatting` · stable · since 0.18.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/rich-text-editor/rich-text-editor.tsx:153`

Make text bold, italic, underlined or code, add headings, quotes, numbered and bulleted lists, and align paragraphs.

- **Where:** Toolbar at the top of the editor of every Long text field, in the form to add or edit a record.
- **How:** Select some text, or place the cursor where you will type, then click a button of the toolbar or press its keyboard shortcut. Click the same button again to remove that formatting.
- **Options:** Text styles: Bold (Mod+B), Italic (Mod+I), Underline (Mod+U), Code (Mod+`). Paragraph types: Heading 1, Heading 2, Quote, Numbered list, Bulleted list. Alignment: left, center, right, justify. Mod is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere; Mod+Z undoes the last change.
- **Rules:** The buttons of the formatting already applied have a grey background. Text styles apply to the selected text, or to what is typed next when nothing is selected. Paragraph types and alignment apply to whole paragraphs: choosing a list turns the selected paragraphs into list items, choosing it again turns them back into paragraphs. The toolbar stays visible at the top of the editor while scrolling. The buttons have icons only, no text.
- **Related:** `field.long-text`

### Date field

`field.date` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/input-supported-types.const.ts:28`

A day, a month or a week, typed or picked from the calendar of the browser.

- **Where:** Project editor: a field with Data type "Date picker" and a "Date format". Filled in the form to add or edit a record; shown in lists and on the details page.
- **How:** In the project editor, give the field the Data type "Date picker" and choose its Date format. In the form of a record, type the date or open the calendar of the browser and pick it. Save the record.
- **Options:** Date format (default Date): Date, a day, shown as year/month/day (e.g. 2026/10/31); Month, a month of a year, shown in short in the language of the browser (e.g. Oct 2026); Week, a week of a year, shown as week-year (e.g. 44-2026).
- **Rules:** The look of the calendar depends on the browser and the device. An empty date is not saved.

### Date & time field

`field.date-time` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/input-supported-types.const.ts:48`

A day with a time of the day, or only a time.

- **Where:** Project editor: a field with Data type "Date & time" and a "Time format". Filled in the form to add or edit a record; shown in lists and on the details page.
- **How:** In the project editor, give the field the Data type "Date & time" and choose its Time format. In the form of a record, type the value or use the picker of the browser. Save the record.
- **Options:** Time format (default Date & time): Date & time, shown as year/month/day hours:minutes on a 24-hour clock (e.g. 2026/10/31 14:30); Time only, shown as typed (e.g. 14:30).
- **Rules:** The time is saved as entered, in the local time of the device, without a time zone. The look of the picker depends on the browser and the device.
