### Check box field

`field.checkbox` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/form-fields/basic-checkbox.component.tsx:10`

A yes/no field, ticked or not, such as "Done" or "Paid".

- **Where:** Project editor: a field with Data type "Check box". Ticked in the form to add or edit a record, and directly in the table view and on the details page.
- **How:** In the project editor, give the field the Data type "Check box". In the form of a record, click the box to tick or untick it. In the table view or on the details page, click the box to change it without opening the form.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** A new record starts with the box not ticked. In the table view and on the details page, clicking the box saves the record (and syncs it) at once. In the tabs of linked records a ticked box is shown as a green check mark and cannot be changed there. If the field is required, a record whose box has never been ticked cannot be saved; once it has been ticked, unticking it is allowed.
- **covers:** `field:basicCheckbox`
- **Related:** `field.required`

### Drop-down list field

`field.drop-down` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/form-fields/basic-select.component.tsx:17`

Pick one value from a list of choices defined for the field, in a drop-down that can be searched.

- **Where:** Project editor: a field with Data type "Drop-down list" and its "Choices". In the form of a record, a box with an arrow; the chosen value is shown as a coloured label in lists and on the details page.
- **How:** Define the choices of the field in the project editor. In the form of a record, click the box or its arrow to open the list and click a choice; type in the box to narrow the list. To clear the field, open the list and click the × next to the chosen item.
- **Options:** The choices of the field (see "Choices of a drop-down or alternative choice"). The field starts empty.
- **Rules:** The chosen item has a check mark in the open list. Typing narrows the list by the value stored for each choice, not by its label: in basic mode the values are numbers (1, 2, 3...), so typing a word may show "Nothing found.". The chosen value is shown as a coloured label; its colour depends on the position of the choice in the list (six colours, repeated), so the same choice always has the same colour. A record whose value no longer matches any choice (e.g. the choice was deleted) shows the field empty. If the field is required, "This field is required" appears when it is left empty.
- **covers:** `field:basicSelect`
- **Related:** `field.choices`, `field.alternative-choice`, `field.required`

### Alternative choice field

`field.alternative-choice` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/form-fields/basic-radio.component.tsx:13`

Pick one value among a few choices, all visible at once as round buttons.

- **Where:** Project editor: a field with Data type "Alternative choice" and its "Choices". In the form of a record, one round button per choice; the chosen value is shown as a coloured label in lists and on the details page.
- **How:** Define the choices of the field in the project editor. In the form of a record, click the round button of the choice.
- **Options:** The choices of the field (see "Choices of a drop-down or alternative choice"). No choice is selected at first.
- **Rules:** Only one choice can be selected. Once a choice is selected the field cannot be emptied again, only changed to another choice. The chosen value is shown like the one of a drop-down list: a label coloured by the position of the choice. Better suited than a drop-down list when the choices are few. If the field is required, "This field is required" appears when it is left empty.
- **covers:** `field:basicRadio`
- **Related:** `field.choices`, `field.drop-down`, `field.required`

### Choices of a drop-down or alternative choice

`field.choices` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/form-fields/options-maker.component.tsx:8`

Define the list of values that can be picked in a Drop-down list or Alternative choice field.

- **Where:** Project editor, in a field with Data type "Drop-down list" or "Alternative choice": the "Choices" box, with a numbered list of choices, the "Add Choice" button and a delete button for each choice.
- **How:** Give the field the Data type "Drop-down list" or "Alternative choice": the "Choices" box appears with two empty choices. Type the Label of each choice. Click "Add Choice" to add another one, or the delete button of a choice ("Delete option" and its number) to remove it. Save the project.
- **Options:** Label of each choice (required). In advanced mode, also the Value stored in the records (by default 1, 2, 3... in the order the choices are added).
- **Rules:** A field always has at least two choices: the delete buttons appear only when there are more than two. Records store the value of the choice, not its label: renaming a label changes how all the records show it, while deleting a choice, or changing its value in advanced mode, leaves the records that had it with an empty field. The project cannot be saved while a choice has no label.
- **Related:** `field.drop-down`, `field.alternative-choice`

### Required fields

`field.required` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/form-validation/validators/required-field.component.tsx:6`

Mark a field as required, so that a record cannot be saved while the field is empty.

- **Where:** Project editor: the "Required" check box of each field. Form to add or edit a record: an asterisk (*) after the label, a message under the field and a message next to the save buttons.
- **How:** In the project editor, tick "Required" on the field and save the project. When filling in a record, fill in the fields marked with an asterisk.
- **Options:** Required: off by default.
- **Rules:** After the field has been left empty, it turns red and shows "This field is required". While a required field is empty the save buttons are disabled, and next to them the form says "To save, fill in the required field: <label>." (or "the required fields:" followed by their labels); the save keyboard shortcut does nothing. Exceptions: on a Long text field the asterisk is shown but saving is not blocked; on a Check box, see the check box field. The first required Short text of type Text can name the records of the section.
- **covers:** `validator:required`
- **Related:** `field.format-validation`, `record.title`

### Check of e-mail, phone and web addresses

`field.format-validation` · stable · since 0.12.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/form-validation/validators-container.component.tsx:11`

Short text fields with Content type Email, Tel or Url check the format of the value and prevent saving until it is correct.

- **Where:** Form to add or edit a record: a red message under the field.
- **How:** Give a Short text field the Content type Email, Tel or Url. When filling in a record, a red message appears under the field while the value has a wrong format and disappears when it is correct.
- **Options:** none: the check depends on the Content type of the field.
- **Rules:** Messages: "Invalid Email" (an address like name@example.com is expected); "Invalid telephone number" (at least ten digits grouped 3-3-4, optionally with a + in front and spaces, dots, dashes or brackets between the groups, e.g. 555 123 4567: numbers with a country code such as +39 in front are not accepted); "Invalid address (it must start with http:// or https://)" (a web address with a domain such as example.com; addresses of a local network such as 192.168.1.1 are not accepted). An empty value passes the check, unless the field is required. While a value is wrong the save buttons are disabled and the form says "To save, correct the fields marked in red.".
- **covers:** `validator:emailFormat`, `validator:telephoneNumber`, `validator:urlFormat`
- **Related:** `field.short-text`, `field.required`

## Link records to each other

<a id="group-link-records"></a>Group `link-records`. **Goal:** Connect related records — the tasks of a project, the projects of a client — and move from one to the other.

**Audience:** Users who have a project with at least two sections and want them connected; may never have heard of relations.

**Notes for writers:** Follow one concrete example: sections "Clients" and "Projects", with Projects as child of Clients. Steps: set "Parent sections" in the editor, add a project and pick its client in "Linked to", open the client and see its projects in a tab, add a new project from the tab (already linked). Screenshots: the "Parent sections:" field, the "Linked to" selector, the details page of the client with the tabs and the collapsed Details panel. Avoid the words parent/child in titles: say "belongs to" (a project belongs to a client); keep the app terms only as labels. Pitfalls: "Linked to" appears only when the parent section has at least one record; a record can be linked to several records, also of different sections; links to deleted records disappear; long texts are not shown in the tabs. Home page: a CRM or project tracker with linked records shows that Anita is more than a list.

### Parent sections

`relation.parent-sections` · stable · since 0.3.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/form-fields/child-of-selector-for-section.component.tsx:24`

Make a section the child of other sections, so that its records can be linked to records of those sections (e.g. Tasks linked to Projects).

- **Where:** Project editor, in the settings of a section: the "Parent sections:" field.
- **How:** In the project editor, open the section that will hold the child records and choose one or more sections in "Parent sections:". Remove a parent with the × on its tag. Save the project.
- **Options:** Any other section of the project; several parent sections are allowed. Default: none.
- **Rules:** The field appears only when the project has at least one other section; a section cannot be its own parent. Once a section has parent sections, the form of its records shows the "Linked to" field, and the records of the parent sections show tabs with the records linked to them.
- **Related:** `relation.link-to-parent`

### Link a record to parent records

`relation.link-to-parent` · stable · since 0.4.0 · `src/app/components/shared-components/forms-automator/form-fields/parents-selector.component.tsx:22`

Connect a record to one or more records of its parent sections, e.g. a task to its project, and open them from its details page.

- **Where:** Form to add or edit a record of a child section: the field "Linked to" followed by the names of the parent sections, at the top of the form. Details page: the links, grouped by parent section, as labels that open the parent record.
- **How:** Open the form of a record of a section that has parent sections. In "Linked to ...", open the list and choose the records (grouped by section and named by their name field); type to search them. Remove a link with the × on its tag. Save the record. A record added from the tab of a parent record is already linked to it.
- **Options:** Any record of the parent sections; several records, also of different sections, can be linked. Default: no link, or the parent record when the record is added from its tab.
- **Rules:** The field appears only when the section has parent sections and at least one of them has records. On the details page each parent section is a row with the name of the section; each link shows the name of the parent record, or "Untitled" when it has none. Links to records that no longer exist are not shown.
- **Related:** `relation.parent-sections`, `record.title`

### Linked records in tabs

`view.child-records-tabs` · stable · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/element/child-records-tabs.component.tsx:147`

On the details of a record, shows the records of the child sections linked to it, one tab per child section (for example the projects of a client).

- **Where:** Details page of a record whose section has child sections: the card under the Details panel, with one tab per child section.
- **How:** Click a tab to see the linked records of that section; click a record (or the arrow at the end of its row) to open it; click "Add to" followed by the section name to add a record already linked to this one.
- **Options:** One tab per child section; the first is selected when the page opens.
- **Rules:** Each tab shows the number of linked records. The table shows up to four short fields, the field that names the records first; long texts and rich text are not shown; ticked checkboxes appear as a check mark. When a tab has no records it reads "No ... linked to this record yet." with an "Add to" button.
- **routes:** `projectSectionEleDetails`
- **Related:** `record.details`, `view.details-panel`, `record.add`

### Collapse the details of a record

`view.details-panel` · stable · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/project/section/element/details.component.tsx:81`

Folds the Details panel of a record, to give room to the tabs of its linked records.

- **Where:** Details page of a record whose section has child sections: the header of the panel, with the chevron on the right.
- **How:** Click anywhere on the header of the panel to collapse it; click again to expand it.
- **Options:** Expanded (default) or collapsed.
- **Rules:** Collapsed, the panel shows only the record title, and the tabs of the linked records move up. The choice is remembered for each section on this device only. The edit button stays available when the panel is collapsed. Sections without child sections have no collapsible header.
- **routes:** `projectSectionEleDetails`
- **Related:** `record.details`, `view.child-records-tabs`

## Keep your projects safe

<a id="group-keep-your-projects-safe"></a>Group `keep-your-projects-safe`. **Goal:** Make sure you never lose a project: choose where it is stored, or keep a backup file you can import again on any device.

**Audience:** Users with at least one project saved only on this device (orange banner) who want a backup or to move it to another device.

**Notes for writers:** Start from the warning users actually see: the orange "This project is saved only on this device" banner, the "Only on this device" badge and "Keep it safe" on the project card. Then the two answers: store it in Dropbox or on a WordPress site (the "Keep your project safe" dialog / "Remote storage"; link to the two sync guides for the details) or export a file with "Data and Structure" and import it again elsewhere. Screenshots: the banner, the "Keep your project safe" dialog, the Export menu with its three options, the Import dialog. Explain the three export scopes in plain words: full backup (can be imported), only the records (for reading elsewhere, cannot be imported), only the structure (to start an empty copy). Pitfalls: "Data Only" files cannot be imported; stopping sync ("Stop syncing with…?") deletes nothing; on iPhone and iPad an app added to the Home Screen has its own data, separate from Safari. Home page: "your data, your choice: only on your device, in your Dropbox or on your WordPress site".

### Warning for projects saved only on this device

`storage.local-only` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/project/local-only-banner.component.tsx:24`

Reminds you that a project not stored in Dropbox or on WordPress exists only in this browser, and offers to save it safely or download a backup.

- **Where:** Orange banner "This project is saved only on this device" at the top of every page of the project; badge "Only on this device" in the header; badge "Only on this device, no backup · Keep it safe" on the project card in the list of projects.
- **How:** Click "Save it in Dropbox or WordPress" (or the header badge) to choose where to keep the project, or "Download a backup" to save a copy of the whole project as a file. Close the banner with the × button.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** The banner shows the date of the last backup ("never" if none). Closing it hides it for that project until the app is reopened; the header badge stays visible. The banner disappears once the project is stored in Dropbox or on a WordPress site.
- **Related:** `storage.choice`

### Choose where a project is stored

`storage.choice` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/remotes/storage-choice.component.tsx:105`

Chooses whether a project is kept in Dropbox, on a WordPress site, in a file on this computer, or only on this device, when creating it, in its settings, or later for a local project.

- **Where:** The storage options when creating a project from a template; "Remote storage" in the project settings; the dialog "Keep your project safe" opened from "Save it in Dropbox or WordPress", the "Only on this device" header badge or "Keep it safe" on a project card.
- **How:** 1. Pick one of the options (the recommended one is marked "Recommended"). 2. For Dropbox, optionally change the folder; for WordPress, choose "Who can see it on the site"; for a new site, type its address. 3. Confirm with the button, whose label says what happens: "Save on <site>", "Save in Dropbox", "Connect Dropbox and save", "Connect and save", "Create and connect Dropbox", "Create and connect WordPress". Choosing a service not yet connected opens its login and brings you back to the project.
- **Options:** Each connected WordPress site where you can create projects, "Dropbox" (or "My Dropbox" if not connected yet), "My WordPress site" / "Another WordPress site" (connect a new site), "A file on this computer" (only in Chromium-based browsers on a computer: selecting it asks where to save the file, "Change" picks another one; the button becomes "Save in the file"), "Only on this device" (not offered when moving a local project). Default: the first connected site, otherwise Dropbox, otherwise this device; Dropbox is recommended when no site is connected. In the project settings, "None: this device only" and "Connect storage" when nothing is connected.
- **Rules:** "Only on this device" is saved only in this browser, with no backup: clearing browsing data, private browsing or losing the device deletes it; it can be moved to Dropbox or WordPress later. Changing or removing the storage of a synced project asks "Stop syncing with <name>?": the project is not deleted, it stays on this device and in Dropbox or on the site. "Not now" closes the dialog. Errors are shown as "The project was not saved" with the message of the service.
- **Related:** `storage.local-only`, `sync.dropbox-projects`, `sync.wordpress-projects`, `sync.wordpress-share`

### Export a project to a file

`export.project` · stable · since 0.13.0 · `src/app/models/project/project-exporter.class.ts:5`

Downloads the project as a JSON file: records and structure, only the records, or only the structure.

- **Where:** "Export" menu on the card of a loaded project (Projects screen) and on the details page of the project.
- **How:** 1. Load the project.
2. Open "Export".
3. Choose "Data and Structure", "Data Only" or "Structure Only": the file is downloaded.
- **Options:** "Data and Structure": a full copy, which can be imported again. "Data Only": only the records, it cannot be imported.
"Structure Only": sections and fields without records, to start a new empty project with the same structure.
- **Rules:** The file is named after the project (name.json). An export with "Data and Structure" counts as a backup: the app
remembers when it was made, for projects saved only on this device.
- **covers:** `export-scope:all`, `export-scope:dataOnly`, `export-scope:structureOnly`
- **Related:** `import.file`, `project.list`

### Import a project from a file

`import.file` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/app/components/projects/project-importer-components/import-project-button.component.tsx:72`

Adds to this device a project saved in an Anita file (a JSON export), with its structure and its records.

- **Where:** "Import" button on the Projects screen, on the "Create a project" page and on the first project page.
- **How:** 1. Click "Import".
2. Choose the .json file.
3. In the "Import project" dialog check or change the name, description and remote storage (where the browser
supports it, the imported file is preselected: see "Keep an imported project in sync with its file").
4. Click "Import".
- **Options:** Name, description and remote storage of the project can be changed before importing.
- **Rules:** Only files exported with "Data and Structure" or "Structure Only" can be imported. Any other file shows "This file
cannot be imported", explaining that exports with "Data Only" do not contain the project structure. An empty file
shows "This file is empty", and a file the browser cannot read "This file cannot be read": both suggest downloading
the file first when it is in a cloud folder and not available offline. Exports of the
previous version of Anita (0.20.0) can be imported. "Import" stays disabled while a required field is empty. The
project is saved in the browser of this device and the Projects list opens.
- **Related:** `export.project`, `project.list`, `project.settings`, `import.file-sync`

## Sync your projects with Dropbox

<a id="group-sync-with-dropbox"></a>Group `sync-with-dropbox`. **Goal:** Connect your Dropbox to have your projects backed up and the same on your computer, phone and tablet.

**Audience:** Users with a Dropbox account and at least one project, who have never connected Anita to anything.

**Notes for writers:** Example: a project created on the computer, saved in Dropbox, then opened on the phone. Steps: Storage and sync → Dropbox → Connect, log in on Dropbox's page, choose Dropbox as storage of a project, check "Synced with Dropbox" and "Last sync", open the app on a second device with the same account (projects of the /Anita folder appear by themselves), "Open from Dropbox" for files in other folders. Screenshots: the Dropbox card (not connected and connected, "Logged in as"), the project page with "Remote storage: Dropbox" and "Sync now", the folder picker, the "is no longer in your Dropbox" dialog. Explain merging in plain words: when the same record was changed on two devices, the most recent change wins. End with "if something goes wrong": the Dropbox messages (not reachable, no space, session expired, file deleted from another device) and what to do; link to "Syncing, logins and sync problems". Pitfalls: one Dropbox account per device; switching account turns the old projects into local ones; disconnecting deletes nothing in Dropbox. Home page: sync across devices with your own Dropbox, no Anita account.

### Connect a Dropbox account

`sync.dropbox-connect` · beta · since 0.18.0 · `src/app/components/remotes/connect-dropbox.component.tsx:10`

Connects your Dropbox to Anita on this device, so that your projects are backed up and available on every device where you connect the same account.

- **Where:** On the "Storage and sync" page (button "Storage and sync" in the list of projects, or the Dropbox and WordPress icons in the header), section Dropbox, button "Connect". Also with "Connect Dropbox and save" / "Create and connect Dropbox" when Dropbox is chosen as storage of a project before connecting it.
- **How:** 1. Open Storage and sync. 2. In the Dropbox card click "Connect": Anita opens the Dropbox login in the same tab. 3. Log in and allow Anita to use your files: Dropbox brings you back to Anita, which shows "Dropbox connected". 4. Choose Dropbox as storage when you create a project, or in its settings ("Remote storage"). To remove the account, click "Disconnect" on the Dropbox card.
- **Options:** When disconnecting with projects of this device synced with Dropbox: "Keep projects" (they stay on this device as local projects) or "Delete from this device"; with no such projects, just "Disconnect". When logging in with a different Dropbox account: "Continue as <name>" or "Cancel".
- **Rules:** One Dropbox account per device; nothing to install. Once connected, the projects of the /Anita folder of the Dropbox are downloaded to this device. The card shows "Logged in as" (name and email), "Projects on this device" and "Status". Disconnecting never deletes anything in Dropbox. Logging in with another account asks "Switch Dropbox account?": the projects of the previous account stop syncing and stay on this device as local projects, so they are not copied to the new account. The login must be completed in the same browser within 30 minutes, otherwise "This connection was not started from this browser, or it took too long. Please connect Dropbox again from Anita." Cancelling on Dropbox shows "The connection was cancelled on Dropbox."; any failure shows "The connection did not complete" with the reason and a "Back to Storage and sync" button. If the login cannot be opened, the card shows "Dropbox cannot be connected" with the reason.
- **routes:** `remotes`, `auth`
- **errors:** `dropbox.authFailed`, `dropbox.network`, `dropbox.unknown`
- **covers:** `cloud:DROPBOX`
- **Related:** `sync.dropbox-projects`, `security.sync-sessions`, `storage.choice`

### Sync projects with Dropbox

`sync.dropbox-projects` · beta · since 0.18.0 · `src/app/libs/cloud-sync/dropbox/dropbox-sync.class.tsx:32`

Keeps each project chosen for Dropbox in a file of your Dropbox and merges the changes made on this device with those made on your other devices.

- **Where:** Chosen as storage of a project: "Dropbox" when creating a project, "Remote storage" in the project settings, or "Save it in Dropbox or WordPress" for a project saved only on this device. The project page shows "Remote storage: Dropbox", the "File" and "Last sync", with a "Sync now" button; the projects list marks it "Synced with Dropbox".
- **How:** 1. Connect Dropbox. 2. Choose Dropbox as storage of a project (optionally pick another folder with "Change"). 3. Work as usual: changes are sent to Dropbox a moment after they are saved, and changes made on other devices are received when the project is opened or checked again. 4. Use "Sync now" on the project page or on the Dropbox card of Storage and sync to sync right away.
- **Options:** Folder of the file: /Anita by default, or any folder chosen with "Change" (Choose a folder: browse, "New folder", "Save in <folder>"). Setting "Remote storage" back to "None: this device only" stops syncing (confirmation "Stop syncing with Dropbox?"): the project stays on this device and in Dropbox.
- **Rules:** Each project is one .json file named after the project title (Dropbox renames it if a file with the same name exists). Projects in the /Anita folder are downloaded automatically on every device connected to the same account; projects saved in other folders are opened on other devices with "Open from Dropbox". Local changes are grouped and sent about 1.5 seconds after the last save. Records are merged one by one using the time of their last change: a record changed on both sides since the last sync keeps the most recent version, and the project page says "N records were changed both on this device and on another one since the last sync. The most recent version was kept." If the file is changed by another device during a sync, the merge is retried up to 3 times. When Dropbox cannot be reached, changes stay on this device ("some changes are not synced yet") and are sent later. Deleting a synced project asks whether to delete its file from Dropbox too: only with "Delete also from Dropbox" the file is moved to the deleted files of Dropbox, where it can be restored for a while (if Dropbox cannot be reached the project is kept on this device); with "Delete from this device only" the file stays and this device no longer downloads it, until it is opened again with "Open from Dropbox". If Dropbox is not connected on the device the project page shows "Dropbox is not connected on this device" and a "Storage and sync" button.
- **errors:** `dropbox.network`, `dropbox.notConnected`, `dropbox.conflict`, `dropbox.insufficientSpace`, `dropbox.rateLimited`, `dropbox.serverError`, `dropbox.invalidFile`, `dropbox.unknown`
- **covers:** `cloud:DROPBOX`
- **Related:** `sync.dropbox-connect`, `sync.dropbox-open-file`, `sync.dropbox-missing-file`, `sync.status`, `sync.automatic`, `storage.choice`

### Open a project from Dropbox

`sync.dropbox-open-file` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/remotes/open-from-dropbox-button.component.tsx:19`

Opens a project file saved anywhere in your Dropbox: the project is added to this device and kept in sync with that file.

- **Where:** Button "Open from Dropbox" in the list of projects, on the page shown when there are no projects, and on the Dropbox card of Storage and sync. Shown only when Dropbox is connected and logged in.
- **How:** 1. Click "Open from Dropbox". 2. In "Open a project from Dropbox" browse the folders (the breadcrumb goes back up). 3. Select the .json file of an Anita project and click "Open project" (or double-click it). 4. The project opens and is synced with that file from then on.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** Only .json files can be selected. If the project is already on this device and not synced, the two copies are merged keeping the records of both. Messages: "<file> is not an Anita project.", "This project is already on this device, synced with <path>.", "This project is already on this device, synced with a WordPress site." Errors are shown in the picker under "The project could not be opened".
- **errors:** `dropbox.invalidFile`, `dropbox.notFound`, `dropbox.network`
- **Related:** `sync.dropbox-projects`

### Projects whose file was deleted from Dropbox

`sync.dropbox-missing-file` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/libs/cloud-sync/dropbox/dropbox-sync.class.tsx:270`

Asks what to do with a project of this device when its file is no longer in your Dropbox, for example because it was deleted from another device.

- **Where:** A dialog titled "<project> is no longer in your Dropbox", shown while syncing with Dropbox.
- **How:** Pick one of the choices of the dialog; closing it asks again at the next session.
- **Options:** "Keep on this device only" (stops syncing, the project becomes local), "Save it again in Dropbox" (creates a new file), "Delete from this device".
- **Rules:** The copy on this device is never deleted without asking. One question at a time is shown, also when several syncs run together. A project deleted on another device with "Delete" is moved to the deleted files of Dropbox, so the other devices show this dialog.
- **errors:** `dropbox.notFound`
- **Related:** `sync.dropbox-projects`

## Store and share projects on a WordPress site

<a id="group-share-on-wordpress"></a>Group `share-on-wordpress`. **Goal:** Keep your projects on your WordPress site and share them with its users, choosing who can see each one.

**Audience:** Users who have (or work with) a WordPress site with the Anita Project Manager plugin; some guides are also for the site administrator who installs the plugin.

**Notes for writers:** Two readers: the administrator (install and activate the Anita Project Manager plugin, add self-hosted copies of Anita in Settings → Anita → Allowed app URLs, assign roles) and the team member (connect the site, open shared projects). Example: a small association's site where the secretary creates a "Members" project and shares it with "Editors and above". Steps: Storage and sync → Connect a WordPress site, type the address, log in on the site, choose the site as storage, pick "Who can see it on the site", see "Visible to" on the project page. Screenshots: the connect card, the WordPress login/authorisation page, the access level choice, the project page for the owner ("you own this project") and for another user ("shared with you"), the "Projects removed from <site>" dialog. Explain what shared users can do: add and edit records, not change the structure or delete the project. End with "if something goes wrong": plugin missing, site not reachable (security plugin or firewall blocking the REST API), address not allowed, "did not allow this change", project removed or no longer shared. Pitfalls: users whose role cannot create projects see "Cannot create projects on this site"; switching account removes projects the new user cannot see. Home page: team sharing with your own WordPress site.

### Connect a WordPress site

`sync.wordpress-connect` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/remotes/connect-wordpress.component.tsx:27`

Connects a WordPress site with the Anita Project Manager plugin, where you can store your projects and share them with the users of the site.

- **Where:** On the "Storage and sync" page (button "Storage and sync" in the list of projects, or the Dropbox and WordPress icons in the header), section "WordPress sites", card "Connect a WordPress site". Also "My WordPress site" / "Another WordPress site" when choosing where to store a project ("Connect and save", "Create and connect WordPress").
- **How:** 1. On the WordPress site, install and activate the free Anita Project Manager plugin (Plugins → Add New). 2. In Anita enter the address of the site and click "Connect": Anita checks the site ("Checking the site…"). 3. Log in with your WordPress account and approve the connection: the site brings you back to Anita, which shows "<site> connected" and downloads the projects you can access. Each connected site gets a card with "Disconnect", "Sync now" and, when needed, "Log in again".
- **Options:** Several sites can be connected. When disconnecting a site with projects on this device: "Keep projects" (they stay as local projects) or "Delete from this device"; otherwise "Disconnect". Logging in with a different account of the same site: "Continue as <name>" or "Cancel".
- **Rules:** The address can be typed without https:// and with admin paths, which are removed. The plugin works with any permalink setting; the data is stored in the database of the site and Anita keeps a copy on this device for offline work. The site card shows "Logged in as" with the WordPress role, "Cannot create projects on this site" when the role is not allowed to, "Projects on this device" and "Status". Disconnecting deletes nothing on the site. Switching account asks "Switch account on <site>?": projects of the previous user that the new one cannot access are removed from this device. Messages: "Enter the address of your WordPress site, for example https://example.com"; "Anita could not reach the Anita Project Manager plugin on <site>…" (check address, plugin, REST API not blocked by a security plugin or firewall); "<site> is a WordPress site, but the Anita Project Manager plugin is not active"; "<site> does not accept connections from this address of Anita (<url>). An administrator of the site can add it in Settings → Anita → Allowed app URLs." (self-hosted copies of Anita must be added there); "The site answered with the address <x>. Connect using that address."; "The connection was cancelled on the WordPress site."; "The answer of the site could not be read. Please connect again."; "This connection was not started from this browser, or it took too long." (30 minutes).
- **routes:** `remotes`, `auth`
- **errors:** `wordpress.network`, `wordpress.pluginMissing`, `wordpress.originNotAllowed`, `wordpress.invalidCode`, `wordpress.unknown`
- **covers:** `cloud:WORDPRESS`
- **Related:** `sync.wordpress-projects`, `sync.wordpress-share`, `security.sync-sessions`, `storage.choice`

### Sync projects with a WordPress site

`sync.wordpress-projects` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/libs/cloud-sync/wordpress/wordpress-sync.class.tsx:33`

Stores a project on a connected WordPress site and keeps this device and the site in sync, record by record.

- **Where:** Chosen as storage of a project: the site when creating a project, "Remote storage" in the project settings, or "Save it in Dropbox or WordPress" for a local project. The project page shows the site, "Visible to", "Last sync" and "Sync now"; the projects list marks it "Synced with <site>"; each site card in Storage and sync has "Sync now".
- **How:** 1. Connect the site. 2. Choose it as storage of a project and choose who can see it. 3. Work as usual: each saved or deleted record is sent to the site right away, and changes made by others or on other devices are merged when the project is opened, checked again, or with "Sync now".
- **Options:** Setting "Remote storage" back to "None: this device only" stops syncing (confirmation "Stop syncing with <site>?"): the project stays on this device and on the site.
- **Rules:** When a project is first linked it is uploaded with all its records; then all the projects of the site visible to you are downloaded to this device (other local projects are not uploaded). If the site already has the project, the two are merged instead of overwritten. Records are merged by the time of their last change: when a record was changed on both sides since the last sync the most recent version is kept, and the project page says "N records were changed both on this device and on <site> since the last sync. The most recent version was kept." The structure (settings and sections) of the site wins, unless an owner or administrator changed it on this device after the last sync: then it is sent to the site, keeping sections added on the site meanwhile. Records of sections no longer on the site stay on this device. When the site cannot be reached, changes stay on this device ("some changes are not synced yet") and are sent at the next sync. If the site is not connected on this device the project page says "This site is not connected on this device". Messages: "<site> could not save the data. Please try again later."; "This project is no longer available on <site>."; otherwise the message of the site or "Something went wrong while syncing with <site>."
- **errors:** `wordpress.network`, `wordpress.dbError`, `wordpress.invalidRequest`, `wordpress.notFound`, `wordpress.unknown`
- **covers:** `cloud:WORDPRESS`
- **Related:** `sync.wordpress-connect`, `sync.wordpress-share`, `sync.wordpress-removed-projects`, `sync.status`, `sync.automatic`, `storage.choice`

### Share a project with the users of a WordPress site

`sync.wordpress-share` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/libs/cloud-sync/wordpress/wordpress.const.ts:15`

Chooses who can see a project stored on a WordPress site, from only you to every registered user, by WordPress role.

- **Where:** "Who can see it on the site" when choosing a WordPress site as storage of a new or local project; the access level next to "Remote storage" in the project settings; "Visible to" on the project page.
- **How:** 1. Choose a WordPress site as storage of the project. 2. Pick who can see it. 3. The users of the site with that role see the project in Anita after connecting the same site.
- **Options:** "Only me" (default), "Administrators", "Editors and above", "Authors and above", "Contributors and above", "All registered users of the site".
- **Rules:** The project page says "you own this project" to its owner, and "shared with you: only its owner or an administrator can change its structure" to the others: they can add and edit records but not edit the project. Only the owner or an administrator can delete a project from the site ("Only the owner of the project or an administrator of the site can delete it."); deleting removes it from the site and from this device, for every user it is shared with. Sites list only users whose role is allowed to create projects as possible storage ("Cannot create projects on this site"). When the site refuses a change: "<site> did not allow this change: <reason>".
- **errors:** `wordpress.forbidden`
- **Related:** `sync.wordpress-projects`, `sync.wordpress-removed-projects`

### Projects removed from a WordPress site

`sync.wordpress-removed-projects` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/libs/cloud-sync/wordpress/wordpress-sync.class.tsx:218`

Handles the projects of this device that a WordPress site no longer returns: deleted on the site, or no longer shared with you.

- **Where:** Dialogs shown while syncing with a site: "Projects removed from <site>" and "<project> is no longer on <site>".
- **How:** Read the list of removed projects and click "OK"; for your own projects pick one of the choices.
- **Options:** For projects you created: "Keep on this device only", "Upload again to <site>" (only if you can create projects on the site), "Delete from this device".
- **Rules:** Projects owned by someone else are removed from this device automatically, then listed in "Projects removed from <site>" ("These projects were deleted on <site>, or their owner stopped sharing them with you"). Your own projects are never deleted without asking ("The copy on this device has not been deleted."). Closing the dialog asks again at the next session. One question at a time is shown.
- **errors:** `wordpress.notFound`
- **Related:** `sync.wordpress-projects`, `sync.wordpress-share`

## Keep a project in a file on your computer

<a id="group-sync-with-a-file"></a>Group `sync-with-a-file`. **Goal:** Save a project in a file of your computer, keep it in sync also when the file is changed outside Anita, and allow Anita to open it at each visit.

**Audience:** Uses Anita on one computer, in Chrome or Edge; wants a file to back up, edit or keep in a folder of their own, without a cloud account.

**Notes for writers:** Explain the browser permission at each visit and the "Allow on every visit" choice (screenshot of the prompt). Say clearly that the project stays only on that computer, and point to Dropbox and WordPress for other devices. Show a manual edit of the JSON being picked up.

### Sync a project with a file on your computer

`sync.local-file-projects` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/libs/cloud-sync/local-file/local-file-sync.class.tsx:24`

Keeps a project saved also in a file of your computer, and reads the changes made to that file outside Anita.

- **Where:** Chosen as storage of a project: "A file on this computer" when creating a project from a template, in "Remote storage" of the project settings, in the dialog "Keep your project safe", or in the "Import project" dialog, where the imported file is chosen already. The project page shows "Remote storage: A file on this computer", the "File" and "Last sync", with "Sync now", "Choose the file" and "Save in a new file"; the projects list marks it "Synced with <file name>".
- **How:** 1. Choose "A file on this computer" and pick where to save the file (when importing, the imported file is used). 2. Each time the project is opened, allow Anita to use the file ("Allow access"). 3. Work as usual: changes are written in the file a moment after they are saved; changes made to the file are read when the project is opened, when the window gets focus and every few seconds.
- **Options:** Where the file is saved and its name (by default the title of the project, in the last folder used). Setting "Remote storage" back to "None: this device only" stops syncing (confirmation "Stop syncing with the file?"): the project stays in the browser and the file stays on the computer.
- **Rules:** Available only in Chromium-based browsers on a computer (Chrome, Edge, Opera...): elsewhere the option is not offered and the project page explains it. The file is a regular Anita export ("Data and Structure") that can be imported anywhere. Records are merged one by one using the time of their last change, as with Dropbox; a record changed by hand in the file, without changing its dates, counts as changed when the file was saved; records added by hand without an id or creation date get them, and are written back to the file; records removed from the file are removed from the project. A file that is not valid JSON, or not an Anita project, is never overwritten: the project page shows "Sync problem" and changes stay in the browser until the file is fixed or a new file is chosen. A file that was moved, renamed or deleted must be chosen again ("Choose the file") or replaced ("Save in a new file"). Deleting the project never deletes the file. The project exists only on this computer: to use it on other devices, store it in Dropbox or on WordPress.
- **errors:** `localFile.unsupported`, `localFile.permissionNeeded`, `localFile.notFound`, `localFile.invalidFile`, `localFile.otherProject`, `localFile.conflict`, `localFile.unknown`
- **covers:** `cloud:LOCAL_FILE`
- **Related:** `sync.local-file-access`, `import.file-sync`, `storage.choice`, `sync.status`, `sync.automatic`

### Keep an imported project in sync with its file

`import.file-sync` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/projects/project-importer-components/import-project-button.component.tsx:58`

When you import a project from a file of your computer, Anita can keep using that file, as it does with Dropbox or WordPress.

- **Where:** "Remote storage" of the "Import project" dialog, preselected on "A file on this computer (<file name>)", with a box explaining how it works.
- **How:** 1. Import a project from a file. 2. Leave "A file on this computer (<file name>)" in "Remote storage", or choose another storage. 3. Click "Import" and allow Anita to edit the file in the browser's prompt.
- **Options:** Keep the file (default), or choose "None: this device only" to import a copy saved only in this browser (the box under the field explains that changes are not written in the file, and that Dropbox or a WordPress site keep the project safe and on all devices), or Dropbox or a WordPress site.
- **Rules:** The file is not asked again: the one chosen with "Import" is used. Offered only in browsers that can use files on the computer (Chrome, Edge and other Chromium-based browsers on a computer); elsewhere the project is imported as a copy, as before. If the permission to edit the file is not granted, the project is imported and the project page asks for it again.
- **errors:** `localFile.permissionNeeded`
- **Related:** `import.file`, `sync.local-file-projects`, `storage.choice`

### Allow Anita to open the file of a project

`sync.local-file-access` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/libs/cloud-sync/local-file/local-file-sync.class.tsx:226`

Asks your permission to read and write the file on your computer that a project is synced with, as browsers require.

- **Where:** A dialog "Allow Anita to open <file>?" when a project synced with a file is opened; then, until allowed, the blue banner "Anita needs your permission to open <file>" at the top of the project pages and a note on the project page.
- **How:** Click "Allow access", then allow it in the browser's prompt. To avoid being asked at every visit, choose "Allow on every visit" in the prompt, when the browser offers it.
- **Options:** "Allow access" or "Not now" in the dialog. In the browser's prompt: allow this time, allow on every visit (where offered), or don't allow.
- **Rules:** Browsers forget the permission when Anita is closed, unless "Allow on every visit" was chosen, so the question comes back at the next visit. Until it is allowed, the project works as usual and its changes are kept in the browser: they are written in the file once allowed. The dialog is shown once per visit for each project; the banner stays until access is allowed.
- **errors:** `localFile.permissionNeeded`
- **Related:** `sync.local-file-projects`

## Syncing, logins and sync problems

<a id="group-sync-status-and-logins"></a>Group `sync-status-and-logins`. **Goal:** Know at a glance whether your projects are synced, what Anita does by itself, and what to do when it asks you to log in again or a sync fails.

**Audience:** Users who have connected Dropbox or a WordPress site (at least one of the two previous guides).

**Notes for writers:** Shared by Dropbox and WordPress: the two sync guides link here for the common part. Explain that syncing is automatic while Anita is open (when it starts, when a project is opened, every minute for the open project, when back online) and that changes made offline or while a login is needed are never lost — they wait on the device. Screenshots: the header icons with their coloured rings (blue syncing, orange failed, red log in again) and tooltips, the status of the cards in Storage and sync, the project page with "Last sync", "some changes are not synced yet", "Sync problem" and "Sync now", the "Log in again" button. Make a small table: what you see → what it means → what to do. Security in plain words: you always log in on Dropbox's or your site's own page, Anita never sees your password, logins stay only in this browser. Pitfall: nothing syncs while the tab is hidden or offline; "Sync now" is hidden while a login is required.

### Automatic sync and working offline

`sync.automatic` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/components/admin-layout/cloud-sync-agent.component.tsx:58`

Syncs Dropbox, the connected WordPress sites and the open project by itself while Anita is open, and keeps the changes on the device while offline.

- **Where:** Nothing to open: it runs in the background whenever Anita is open in a browser tab.
- **How:** Nothing to do: keep working, also offline. Use "Sync now" to sync immediately.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** Projects synced with a file on this computer are checked every 5 seconds and when the window gets focus, also offline. Syncs at start, when a service is connected or a login is renewed, when a project is opened, every 5 minutes for the list of projects of each service, every minute (and when the window gets focus, at most every 15 seconds) for changes to the open project, and when the device goes back online. Nothing is synced while the tab is hidden or the device is offline, and services that need a new login are skipped. Changes made offline are kept on this device and sent at the next sync. Messages: "Anita could not reach Dropbox. Your changes are kept on this device and will be synced when Dropbox is reachable again."; "Anita could not reach <site>. Your changes are kept on this device and will be synced when the site is reachable again."
- **errors:** `dropbox.network`, `wordpress.network`
- **Related:** `sync.status`, `sync.dropbox-projects`, `sync.wordpress-projects`

### Sync status and problems

`sync.status` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/state/sync/sync-state.atoms.ts:6`

Shows whether Dropbox, each WordPress site and the open project are synced, syncing, waiting for a login or failed, and what was resolved in the last sync.

- **Where:** Header: the Dropbox icon and one icon per connected site (tooltip and colored ring), opening Storage and sync. Storage and sync: "Status" of each card. Project page: "Last sync", "Sync problem" and "Synced" notes.
- **How:** Look at the header icons; hover them for the status; click them to open Storage and sync. On the project page read "Last sync" and click "Sync now" to sync right away.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** Header tooltips: "<service>: synced", "<service>: syncing…" (blue pulsing ring), "<service>: last sync failed" (orange ring), "<service>: log in again to resume syncing" (red ring). Card status: "Connected", "Syncing…", "Synced on <date, time>", "Login required", with the alert "Last sync failed" or "Log in again to resume syncing". Project page: "Not synced yet", "Syncing…" or the date of the last sync, plus "some changes are not synced yet" when local changes are waiting; "Sync problem" shows the message of the last failure; "Synced" reports the records changed on both sides, of which the most recent version was kept. "Sync now" is hidden while a login is required.
- **routes:** `remotes`
- **Related:** `sync.automatic`, `sync.dropbox-projects`, `sync.wordpress-projects`, `security.sync-sessions`

### Logins to Dropbox and WordPress sites

`security.sync-sessions` · beta · since 1.0.0 · `src/app/libs/cloud-sync/wordpress/wordpress-auth.class.ts:59`

Keeps your Dropbox and WordPress logins secure on this device and asks you to log in again when a session expires or is revoked, without losing changes.

- **Where:** "Log in again" on the Dropbox or site card of Storage and sync and on the project page ("Log in to Dropbox again", "Log in to <site> again"); red ring on the header icon.
- **How:** When "Login required" appears, click "Log in again", log in on Dropbox or on the site and come back to Anita: syncing resumes and pending changes are sent.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** You always log in on the page of Dropbox or of the site: Anita never sees your password. The connection uses a single-use code checked against the browser that started it (PKCE), valid 30 minutes, and the answer must come from the site that was checked. Access tokens are stored only in this browser and renewed automatically; disconnecting forgets them (on Dropbox they are also revoked). While a login is required, changes are kept on this device. Messages: "Your Dropbox session has expired or was disconnected. Log in again to resume syncing; your changes are kept on this device."; "Dropbox is not connected on this device. Connect it to sync this project; until then, changes are saved on this device only."; "Your session on <site> has expired. Log in again to resume syncing; your changes are kept on this device."; "This device was disconnected from <site>, for example because your password was changed. Log in again to resume syncing."
- **routes:** `auth`, `remotes`
- **errors:** `dropbox.authFailed`, `dropbox.missingScope`, `dropbox.notConnected`, `wordpress.unauthorized`, `wordpress.tokenExpired`, `wordpress.tokenInvalid`, `wordpress.tokenRevoked`, `wordpress.notConnected`, `wordpress.invalidCode`
- **Related:** `sync.dropbox-connect`, `sync.wordpress-connect`, `sync.status`

## Use Anita as an app, also offline

<a id="group-anita-on-your-devices"></a>Group `anita-on-your-devices`. **Goal:** Install Anita on your computer or phone like any other app, use it without an internet connection and always have the latest version.

**Audience:** Any user; best read after the first project, when Anita becomes a daily tool.

**Notes for writers:** Home page material: works offline and can be installed, no app store needed. Steps per platform with screenshots: Chrome / Edge on a computer (install icon in the address bar), Android ("Install app"), iPhone and iPad (Safari → Share → "Add to Home Screen"). Explain offline simply: after the first visit everything opens without internet; only syncing and connecting accounts need it. Updates: automatic, used after all Anita tabs and windows are closed, never touch your data; the version is at the bottom of the sidebar. Important pitfall for iPhone and iPad: the app added to the Home Screen keeps its own data, separate from Safari, and removing it can delete that data — sync or export first.

### Install Anita as an app

`app.install` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/serviceWorkerRegistration.ts:11`

Add Anita to the home screen, dock or start menu and open it in its own window like any other app.

- **Where:** The browser's install option (install icon in the address bar, or "Add to Home Screen" / "Install app" in the browser menu) while Anita is open.
- **How:** 1. Open Anita in a browser that supports installing web apps (for example Chrome, Edge, Safari on iPhone and iPad).
2. Choose "Install" or "Add to Home Screen" in the browser.
3. Open Anita from its icon: it starts on the projects list in its own window, without the browser bars.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** The installed app is the same Anita as the web page, works offline and gets the same updates.
On computers and Android the installed app usually shares the data of the browser it was installed from; on iPhone and iPad an app added to the Home Screen keeps its own data, separate from Safari, and removing it can delete that data: sync or export your projects to move them between the two.
Installing needs a browser that supports it; in the others Anita keeps working as a normal web page.
- **Related:** `app.offline`, `app.updates`, `storage.local-database`

### Use Anita offline

`app.offline` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/service-worker.ts:16`

After the first visit Anita opens and works without an internet connection.

- **Where:** Automatic, in the browser and in the installed app.
- **How:** 1. Open Anita once while online: the app is saved on the device.
2. Later, open it without a connection: your projects and records are there and can be viewed and edited.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** The app itself (pages, styles, code) is kept on the device; your data is always on the device anyway (see "Where your data is kept").
Every address of Anita opens offline, including links to a record.
What needs the internet does not work offline: syncing with Dropbox or WordPress, connecting an account, opening links to other sites. Changes made offline stay on the device and can be synced when you are back online.
- **Related:** `app.install`, `app.updates`, `storage.local-database`

### App updates

`app.updates` · stable · since 0.1.0 · `src/serviceWorkerRegistration.ts:41`

New versions of Anita are downloaded automatically and used the next time the app is opened.

- **Where:** Automatic; the version in use is shown at the bottom of the sidebar.
- **How:** Nothing to do. To start using a new version, close every tab and window of Anita (also the installed app) and open it again.
- **Options:** none
- **Rules:** When you open Anita while online, it checks for a new version and downloads it in the background.
The new version is used only after all the tabs and windows of Anita have been closed; until then the current one keeps running. No message is shown when an update is ready.
Updates never touch your data, which stays in the browser.
- **Related:** `app.offline`, `app.install`
